about: Historical context for The Count of Monte Cristo: the real political events that set the plot going.

match: lose a day and a half at the Island of Elba
entries.modern: Napoleon was exiled to Elba in May 1814 and left it on 26 February 1815; Dantès's errand there (February 1815) and the letter he carries to a Bonapartist in Paris put him in the middle of the plot to return.
sources: Philip Dwyer, Napoleon: Passion, Death and Resurrection 1815–1840 (2018)
entries.relationship: Real background; the Pharaon's call at Elba is fiction.

match: after the Hundred Days and after Waterloo
entries.modern: Napoleon returned to power on 20 March 1815 and was defeated at Waterloo on 18 June 1815; Louis XVIII was restored on 8 July — the 'Hundred Days'.
entries.relationship: Real events; Dantès stays forgotten in the Château d'If through them (fiction).
